section_summary: This section covers Saburo Kurusu’s appeal against his purge designation, Prime Minister Katayama’s account of party and economic problems, and Japanese ministers’ views on coalition politics, aid, labor and government staffing. It also contains British parliamentary debate extracts on Japan’s occupation and recovery, a State Department telegram on explaining U.S. policy in China, and a Chinese news agency article criticizing the occupation’s re-education efforts. Two incoming telegrams have little or no legible substantive text.

subfiles.title: Appeal by ex-Ambassador Kurusu against Disqualification from Office
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Forwards Kurusu’s appeal against his purge designation.
subfiles.summary: Sebald sends Kurusu’s confidential appeal and notes his concern that Japanese authorities have not referred it to GHQ.

subfiles.title: Appeal for Examination of Qualification for Public Offices
subfiles.about: Kurusu requests individual review and removal of his purge designation.
subfiles.summary: Kurusu argues that service as ambassador to Germany should not automatically establish that he promoted militarism. He recounts opposing a military alliance, being excluded from Tripartite Pact negotiations, and seeking resignation after signing on instruction. He asks that diplomatic records and former colleagues be consulted.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Katayama Tetsu, Prime Minister
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Reports Katayama’s views on party divisions, labor and Japan’s economic difficulties.
subfiles.summary: Katayama expected the Social Democratic right wing to prevail, but the party subsequently repudiated its four-party agreement. He discussed war bond interest, unions, coalition constraints, vote buying, inflation and administrative reform.

subfiles.title: 29-Man Executive Body Elected by Socialists
subfiles.about: Lists the newly elected Social Democratic Party Central Executive Committee.
subfiles.summary: The right wing won 17 seats and the left wing 12; one seat remained vacant.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Extracts from Foreign Policy Debate in Commons on Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards Hansard extracts on Japan from the January 22–23 Commons debate.
subfiles.summary: The embassy highlights Bevin’s preference for a broad peace conference and Teeling’s and Paton’s discussion of occupation policy.

subfiles.title: Bevin on the Japanese Peace Treaty
subfiles.about: Argues for a Japanese peace conference including the countries that fought Japan.
subfiles.summary: Bevin rejects giving the Soviet Union a predominant role through the Council of Foreign Ministers.

subfiles.title: G. Lang on American Work in Japan
subfiles.about: Comments briefly on American occupation work in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Lang says his visits showed no evidence that America sought to crush democracy in Japan.

subfiles.title: William Teeling on British Policy in Japan
subfiles.about: Questions British policy toward Japan’s economy, occupation and future trade.
subfiles.summary: Teeling presses ministers on zaibatsu dissolution, purges, textile competition and withdrawal of British troops. He argues that weak British engagement may reduce its influence over Japan’s future trade and peace settlement.

subfiles.title: John Paton on Japanese Democracy and Economic Recovery
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan’s political reforms and the economic basis for their survival.
subfiles.summary: Paton praises the occupation’s political and agrarian reforms while finding economic policy uncertain. He argues that lasting democracy and peace require an economy able to sustain a decent standard of living.

subfiles.title: Wingfield Digby on Soviet Influence in Asia
subfiles.about: Comments on Soviet influence in northern Korea, Mongolia and Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Digby describes expanded Soviet influence while distinguishing Chinese from Russian communists.

subfiles.title: Press Material Explaining U.S. Policies in Japan
subfiles.to: American Consulate General, Shanghai; repeated to Nanking and Tokyo
subfiles.about: Addresses requests for information to counter Chinese criticism of U.S. policy in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department describes material supplied to Shanghai and seeks attributable policy explanations addressing criticism in East Asia. It asks whether Asian editors should be invited to visit Japan.

subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram, Control 2779
subfiles.about: Surviving pages show only a telegram header and illegible material.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Japanese Minister of Communications
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Forwards a memorandum on political, economic and labor discussions with Japanese ministers.
subfiles.summary: Sebald identifies aid, party politics, communist union activity and strike law as principal topics.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with Miki, Matsumoto and Suzuki
subfiles.from: W. Henry Lawrence Jr. and Rolland H. Bushner
subfiles.about: Records Japanese ministers’ views on U.S. aid, party alignments, administration and labor disputes.
subfiles.summary: Miki welcomes the U.S. aid announcement and describes plans for economic rehabilitation. The ministers discuss party realignment, a Diet member’s arrest, Japan’s attendance at frequency board meetings and communications staffing. Miki alleges communist activity in labor bodies and urges a clearer legal definition of strikes.

subfiles.title: Government Releases Adjustment Plan
subfiles.about: Describes the Japanese government’s plan to reduce and reorganize civil service staffing.
subfiles.summary: The plan calls for a general 25 percent reduction in budgeted personnel, with separate treatment for government enterprises and specified occupations. Ministries must submit plans by mid-February.

subfiles.title: Re-Education of Japan Seen a Failure?
subfiles.about: Forwards a Central News Agency article critical of occupation policy.
subfiles.summary: The consulate treats the agency handout as evidence of criticism from a section of the Kuomintang government.

subfiles.title: Re-Education of Japan Seen a Failure?
subfiles.about: Questions whether U.S. occupation reforms have changed Japanese political attitudes.
subfiles.summary: Shen argues that outward cooperation masks enduring nationalism and hostility to the occupation. He criticizes Japanese leaders and parties, doubts adult re-education efforts, and objects to attempts to romanize Japanese. The article warns that militarism could return without deeper changes in attitudes.

subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram, Control 3755
subfiles.about: The page contains routing information for an incoming telegram with no legible message body.
subfiles.summary: Only header, receipt and routing details are visible.
